markdown_report:
The best next experiment is a small, calibrated recent-transition residual on unchanged SASRec. At 10% progress, this offers a cheaper, more identifiable test than another learned fusion architecture. No improvement is established.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Normalized convex fusion scored 0.4000 versus the supplied baseline’s 0.5050. This weakens that particular implementation, without isolating whether normalization, pooling, or gating caused the difference. (2) Users report both stale-interest persistence and broad associations displacing specific current interests. Recent directed transitions could address these distinct failures, but cannot establish compatibility. (3) Electronics has 22.3% negative training margins. This motivates discrimination experiments, although training separation does not predict validation HR@10.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Petrov et al. report competitive history-aware transition models under different datasets and evaluation conditions [1]. Their findings justify testing counts here, not assuming transfer. (2) Scalable CE and gSASRec motivate objective changes [2,3]. Stronger negative pressure can nevertheless suppress plausible interests. (3) SComGNN distinguishes complementary relationships from simple similarity [4]. Available histories cannot reliably identify duplicate functions or specification compatibility.

**Framework.** Three directions separate evidence sources from learning mechanisms:

| Direction | Evidence | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Recent transitions | Ordered training interactions | Sparse support and popularity shortcuts |
| Ranking objectives | Observed next items versus sampled negatives | False negatives and compute cost |
| Content augmentation | Permitted titles/descriptions | Similarity does not establish usefulness |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are 0–10; difficulty increases with implementation burden. Each cell gives a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-transition residual [1] | 3: diagnosis-specific; established counts | 7: modular; sparsity | 8: timely specificity; no compatibility proof | 6: alternative ranking evidence; complementarity untested | 3: sparse counts; calibration care |
| Uniform 32-negative CE [2,3] | 2: controlled adaptation; standard loss | 7: reusable; sampling-sensitive | 4: better discrimination possible; no temporal mechanism | 8: targets misranking; training-only evidence | 3: vectorizable; memory cost |
| Lexical feature augmentation [4] | 3: accessible content; established hybrid | 6: sparse-item support; noisy text | 5: specific descriptors; similarity ambiguity | 5: extra evidence; no diagnosed content deficit | 5: no pretraining; pipeline changes |

**Selected algorithm.** Count adjacent training transitions and smooth sparse rows toward uniform probability. Average transition distributions from the latest five source items with fixed recency decay. Add their centered, training-scale-normalized log probabilities to frozen SASRec scores using one validation-selected coefficient, including zero.

This explicitly targets stale historical influence and overly broad immediate recommendations; it also tests whether directed behavioral evidence corrects neural misranking. These are mechanisms, not demonstrated outcomes. Compare SASRec-only, transition-only, last-item residual, and recent-five residual under bounded compute. Select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Report per-category outcomes; retain full-catalog unseen recommendations for the twenty simulator users. Compatibility and duplicate-function failures remain unresolved.

idea.description: Add a calibrated recency-weighted sparse transition residual to the unchanged per-dataset SASRec predictor. Initially use fixed fusion coefficients rather than a learned confidence gate, preserving a zero-coefficient baseline.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale historical influence and broad associations displacing specific recent interests. Recent directed transitions provide an explicit local behavioral signal addressing both. Electronics’ 22.3% negative neural training margins and Industrial_and_Scientific’s 10.68% motivate testing complementary ranking evidence, but do not establish that transition fusion will improve held-out ranking. The supplied normalized-fusion result of 0.4000 versus baseline 0.5050 favors preserving the baseline while testing a simpler addition.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], unchanged splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, independent models and all four dataset routes. Respect the effective SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. All artifacts belong beneath the trial directory; execution remains single-GPU and all training, calibration, diagnostics, debugging and failures count toward the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

For each category, count adjacent pairs only from training histories: C[i,j], with source totals n[i]. For N nonpadding items, use P(j|i)=(C[i,j]+lambda/N)/(n[i]+lambda), initially lambda=10 as a declared experimental setting, not an established optimum. For the last at most five observed items, weight occurrences by 0.5 raised to their distance from the final item and normalize the weights. Repeated occurrences retain their individual weights. Define P_recent(j|prefix) as the weighted average of these smoothed rows. Unsupported source rows are uniform. Empty prefixes receive a zero residual.

Define t=log(P_recent), centered by its mean across the complete nonpadding catalog for that prefix. Compute neural and transition standard deviations from a fixed seed-42 sample of training prefixes and uniform catalog candidates, using the same candidate identities for both components. Freeze these scales before validation and bound denominators away from zero. Score s=s_neural+alpha*(sigma_neural/sigma_transition)*t_centered. Test alpha in {0,0.1,0.3}; candidate-independent centering cannot affect ranks. Keep sparse counts and uniform row offsets instead of materializing an N-by-N matrix. Use identical formulas for sampled-candidate and full-catalog inference.

First compare the unchanged baseline, transition-only, and last-item/recent-five residuals. Avoid adding an objective change until this comparison is resolved. Select a single shared configuration across the four categories by host-computed macro validation HR@10; break ties toward alpha=0 and then the simpler configuration. Report actual cost and completed controls without claiming results for unrun comparisons. No test labels or hidden files may be accessed.

Update the predictor writer so working/predict.py loads each category’s SASRec checkpoint, sparse transition counts, smoothing constant, history window, decay, frozen scales, and selected coefficient. Preserve identical routing and scoring during validation, final inference, and full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and metric_definitions. Keep view.model as the actual SASRec nn.Module and preserve item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, and review_data compatibility. Label existing margins as neural-only. Add a separate fused probe only when actual prefix histories and frozen fusion artifacts are available; otherwise return null with an explicit reason. For a queried adjacent occurrence, subtract its contribution from C[source,target] and the source total before recomputing the affected transition probabilities. Report this as an in-sample leave-one-occurrence-out count diagnostic, not an out-of-sample neural evaluation. Do not reconstruct prefixes ambiguously from repeated item IDs. Investigate the single CDs_and_Vinyl suffix-audit failure before attributing any change to improved causality. Use no unavailable metadata or inferred simulator traits; title similarity and transition evidence cannot certify compatibility or redundant ownership.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in FOUR_DATASETS:
    model = unchanged_per_dataset_SASRec(seed=42)
    train_with_original_protocol(default_epochs=200)
    counts = sparse_adjacent_counts(training_histories_only)
    scales = frozen_scales_from_fixed_training_prefix_candidate_sample(seed=42)
    save_under_trial(model, counts, scales)

for configuration in predeclared_bounded_configurations:
    # baseline, transition-only, last-item residual, recent-five residual
    for category in FOUR_DATASETS:
        for prefix, candidates in existing_host_validation_protocol:
            neural = model.score(prefix, candidates)
            rows = smoothed_transition_rows(last_items(prefix, configuration.window))
            probability = recency_weighted_average(rows, decay=0.5)
            transition = log(probability[candidates]) - full_catalog_mean_log(probability)
            score = configured_combination(neural, transition, frozen_scales)
    # Host computes the unchanged pinned macro HR@10.
select_shared_configuration_using_only_host_validation_HR10()
write_predictor_with_exact_category_artifacts_and_scoring()
run_measured_compatible_diagnostics_and_native_full_catalog_recommendations()
# Enforce the aggregate GPU-second budget throughout.

originality.positive: A diagnosis-driven, baseline-preserving test of recent directed evidence with explicit calibration and self-count controls.
originality.negative: Transition counts, recency weighting, smoothing and score fusion are established methods; novelty is incremental.

future_potential.positive: A cheap modular experiment can establish whether neural and transition evidence are complementary before learning confidence gates.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transitions and popularity effects may limit transfer, and the method cannot establish functional compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: The SASRec architecture and training objective remain unchanged; sparse count artifacts support inexpensive residual scoring.
code_difficulty.negative: Full-catalog scoring parity, frozen calibration, generated predictor loading and occurrence-aware diagnostics require care.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
contributions: [1] Supplied search summary describes smoothed, history-aware transition models with recency weighting and competitive results against sequential neural models.
limitations: Different datasets and NDCG@10 protocol; no demonstrated gain for this benchmark or SASRec-transition fusion.

related_work.title: Scalable Cross-Entropy
contributions: [2] Approximates full cross-entropy using informative catalog subsets.
limitations: Does not establish that uniform sampled CE improves the four-category sampled HR@10 task.

related_work.title: gSASRec: Generalized Binary Cross-Entropy for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: [3] Motivates correcting overconfidence associated with negative sampling.
limitations: Generalized BCE is a separate objective intervention and does not validate transition fusion.

related_work.title: SComGNN
contributions: [4] Models complementary relationships through both relatedness and dissimilarity.
limitations: Does not justify interpreting lexical similarity or observed sequential transitions as verified compatibility.
